newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to discuss railway privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to discuss railway privatisation.

text.p: The Lithuanian transport ministry is due this week to discuss a plan to privatise some 30 percent of the country's national railway, the ministry said on Monday.
The ministry will discuss its privatisation list on Tuesday.

"The transport ministry is going to suggest to the government to include the 100 percent state-owned Lithuanian railways on the privatisation list and to privatise up to 30 percent of this special purpose company," transport ministry council secretary Vaclovas Narbutas told Reuters.
Lithuanian railways has share capital of 1.2 billion litas ($300.2 million).
"The railway lines and supporting systems will not be privatised at this stage," Narbutas added.
But he said state-owned Lithuanian Airlines was so far not on the 1997 privatisation list, which includes 42 companies.
He said the prevailing opinion was that airport runways, railroad lines and port quays should stay in state hands.
The new right-wing government of Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has promised to speed privatisation in Lithuania, viewed as lagging behind that of neighbours, Latvia and Estonia.
But the government has so far committed itself to selling only the state-owned telecoms firm.
